    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN

// gh-1478 — daily-publish self-filer: signal-first failure excerpts,
// cancelled-run digests, root-cause dedup (2026-10-10 morning incidents:
// #1472 cancelled leg filed an empty shrug, #1473 quoted the pub.dev
// file-tree listing while the real server message sat one screen above,
// and #1473 re-filed a root cause already open as #1452).
//
// Behavioral coverage in the release_flow_race_test.dart style: stubbed
// `gh` on PATH answering run-view/search/issue calls from per-test fixture
// files (the stub fails loudly on unknown commands so script drift turns
// red), then scripts/daily_publish_report.sh run end-to-end with the LEG_*
// env wiring the daily-publish.yml report job sets.
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:test/test.dart';

final _fixtureRoot = Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('daily-report-');

/// One stubbed-gh sandbox: `bin/gh` answers from `$GH_STUB_DIR` fixtures
/// and logs every invocation to `$GH_LOG_FILE`.
class ReportRun {
  ReportRun(
    this.exitCode,
    this.output,
    this.summary,
    this.ghLog,
    this.createdBody,
    this.comments,
    this.dir,
  );

  final int exitCode;
  final String output; // stdout+stderr of the report script
  final String summary; // GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY content
  final List<String> ghLog; // every stubbed gh invocation
  final String createdBody; // body of the created issue ('' = none created)
  final String comments; // concatenated comment bodies per issue
  final String dir; // fixture dir (debugging)

  bool get created => createdBody.isNotEmpty;
  bool get commented => comments.isNotEmpty;

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id

  local existing

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"
}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1480
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1480
- **Title**: gh-1478 [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1478` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +870
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:33:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T09:21:18Z

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1480._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: test gap — no coverage for the CLI leg's ceiling lookup**

The cancelled-leg test only exercises the TestFlight shape, and the wiring test greps for the mere presence of the `leg_ceiling_minutes` string — so the regex bug above (CLI fragment with `+` never matches the workflow yaml) passes CI silently. A small addition would have caught it:

```dart
test('ceiling lookup handles the CLI leg name with a literal +', () {
  final r = runReport(
    'cancelled-cli',
    legResults: const {'cli': 'cancelled'},
    fixtures: const {'run-555.json': _run555Jobs},
    withWorkflowYaml: true,
  );
  expect(r.createdBody, contains('Timeout ceiling'),
      reason: 'the CLI leg name contains + which must match literally');
});
```

Alternatively (or additionally) assert in the existing wiring test that the fixture yaml's `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` ceiling (360) is resolvable.

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `fmt_elapsed` doc comment promises zero-padding the code doesn't produce**

The comment says `-> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"`, but the arithmetic emits unpadded components: 3723s renders as `1h2m3s`, not `1h02m03s`. Purely cosmetic (the cancelled-digest readers won't care), but the comment documents a format the code doesn't implement — either pad (`printf '%dh%02dm%02ds'`) or fix the comment to say `1h2m3s`.

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# gh-1478: [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)

## Description

## Problem

The daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh` + the Summary job) files issues whose "Last lines of the failed step's log" are systematically useless — proven twice in one morning (2026-10-10):

1. **#1472** (testflight): the leg run was `cancelled` (job hit its own timeout mid-checkout) → digest body says *"(no failed-step log available — see the run link)"*. A cancelled job produces no failed step, so the one thing the reader needs — WHICH job hit WHAT limit — is absent.
2. **#1473** (pubdev): the digest quoted the `dart pub publish` **file-tree listing** as the tail; the actual failure — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — sat one screen above. The extractor grabbed noise over signal.
3. **No root-cause dedup**: #1473 re-filed a failure whose root cause was already open as #1452 (CHANGELOG > 256 KiB). Same failure will re-file every day until #1452 lands, spamming the tracker with symptom duplicates.

## Requirements

1. **Signal-first excerpt**: when building the digest, grep the failed job's log for `::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines (priority order) and quote the first matches with a few lines of context; fall back to the raw tail only when no signal line exists.
2. **Cancelled-run handling**: a leg whose run concluded `cancelled` gets a dedicated digest section — which job was in flight, its `timeout-minutes`, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of the empty "no failed-step log" shrug.
3. **Root-cause dedup**: before filing, match the extracted error signature (normalized, e.g. the server message / ::error:: text hash) against open issues' bodies/comments; if a match exists, comment on that issue with the new run link instead of filing a new one. Leg-title dedup alone is not enough (#1452 vs #1473).
4. Keep the existing auto-close-on-green and dedup-by-open-leg-issue behavior.

## Tests

- Fixture-driven unit tests for the extractor: tree-noise log → quotes the server message; cancelled-run log set → cancelled section with job+ceiling; no-signal log → tail fallback.
- Dedup test: open issue containing the same signature → comment, not new issue.
- The `inject_failure` TEST hook in daily-publish.yml already exercises the filing path end-to-end — extend it to assert the excerpt content, not just issue creation.

## Evidence

- #1472 body (empty digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- #1473 body (tree-noise digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1473#issuecomment-6095262585
- Root cause already open elsewhere: #1452

## Machine jobs

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {

      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then

  else
    local created

      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id
  local title="[daily-publish] $1 leg failed"
  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ leg \`$1\` went green again in $daily_url — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    actions+="auto-closed #${existing} ($1 green again)"$'\n'
  fi
}

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"
}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1480
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1480
- **Title**: gh-1478 [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1478` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +870
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:33:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T09:21:18Z

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1480._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: test gap — no coverage for the CLI leg's ceiling lookup**

The cancelled-leg test only exercises the TestFlight shape, and the wiring test greps for the mere presence of the `leg_ceiling_minutes` string — so the regex bug above (CLI fragment with `+` never matches the workflow yaml) passes CI silently. A small addition would have caught it:

```dart
test('ceiling lookup handles the CLI leg name with a literal +', () {
  final r = runReport(
    'cancelled-cli',
    legResults: const {'cli': 'cancelled'},
    fixtures: const {'run-555.json': _run555Jobs},
    withWorkflowYaml: true,
  );
  expect(r.createdBody, contains('Timeout ceiling'),
      reason: 'the CLI leg name contains + which must match literally');
});
```

Alternatively (or additionally) assert in the existing wiring test that the fixture yaml's `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` ceiling (360) is resolvable.

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `fmt_elapsed` doc comment promises zero-padding the code doesn't produce**

The comment says `-> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"`, but the arithmetic emits unpadded components: 3723s renders as `1h2m3s`, not `1h02m03s`. Purely cosmetic (the cancelled-digest readers won't care), but the comment documents a format the code doesn't implement — either pad (`printf '%dh%02dm%02ds'`) or fix the comment to say `1h2m3s`.

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# gh-1478: [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)

## Description

## Problem

The daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh` + the Summary job) files issues whose "Last lines of the failed step's log" are systematically useless — proven twice in one morning (2026-10-10):

1. **#1472** (testflight): the leg run was `cancelled` (job hit its own timeout mid-checkout) → digest body says *"(no failed-step log available — see the run link)"*. A cancelled job produces no failed step, so the one thing the reader needs — WHICH job hit WHAT limit — is absent.
2. **#1473** (pubdev): the digest quoted the `dart pub publish` **file-tree listing** as the tail; the actual failure — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — sat one screen above. The extractor grabbed noise over signal.
3. **No root-cause dedup**: #1473 re-filed a failure whose root cause was already open as #1452 (CHANGELOG > 256 KiB). Same failure will re-file every day until #1452 lands, spamming the tracker with symptom duplicates.

## Requirements

1. **Signal-first excerpt**: when building the digest, grep the failed job's log for `::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines (priority order) and quote the first matches with a few lines of context; fall back to the raw tail only when no signal line exists.
2. **Cancelled-run handling**: a leg whose run concluded `cancelled` gets a dedicated digest section — which job was in flight, its `timeout-minutes`, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of the empty "no failed-step log" shrug.
3. **Root-cause dedup**: before filing, match the extracted error signature (normalized, e.g. the server message / ::error:: text hash) against open issues' bodies/comments; if a match exists, comment on that issue with the new run link instead of filing a new one. Leg-title dedup alone is not enough (#1452 vs #1473).
4. Keep the existing auto-close-on-green and dedup-by-open-leg-issue behavior.

## Tests

- Fixture-driven unit tests for the extractor: tree-noise log → quotes the server message; cancelled-run log set → cancelled section with job+ceiling; no-signal log → tail fallback.
- Dedup test: open issue containing the same signature → comment, not new issue.
- The `inject_failure` TEST hook in daily-publish.yml already exercises the filing path end-to-end — extend it to assert the excerpt content, not just issue creation.

## Evidence

- #1472 body (empty digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- #1473 body (tree-noise digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1473#issuecomment-6095262585
- Root cause already open elsewhere: #1452

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"
}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1480
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1480
- **Title**: gh-1478 [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1478` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +870
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:33:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T09:21:18Z

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml

```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml

```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):


### Thread 2 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk

```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

blocks.text:
# gh-1478: [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)

## Description

## Problem

The daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh` + the Summary job) files issues whose "Last lines of the failed step's log" are systematically useless — proven twice in one morning (2026-10-10):

1. **#1472** (testflight): the leg run was `cancelled` (job hit its own timeout mid-checkout) → digest body says *"(no failed-step log available — see the run link)"*. A cancelled job produces no failed step, so the one thing the reader needs — WHICH job hit WHAT limit — is absent.
2. **#1473** (pubdev): the digest quoted the `dart pub publish` **file-tree listing** as the tail; the actual failure — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — sat one screen above. The extractor grabbed noise over signal.
3. **No root-cause dedup**: #1473 re-filed a failure whose root cause was already open as #1452 (CHANGELOG > 256 KiB). Same failure will re-file every day until #1452 lands, spamming the tracker with symptom duplicates.

## Requirements

1. **Signal-first excerpt**: when building the digest, grep the failed job's log for `::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines (priority order) and quote the first matches with a few lines of context; fall back to the raw tail only when no signal line exists.
2. **Cancelled-run handling**: a leg whose run concluded `cancelled` gets a dedicated digest section — which job was in flight, its `timeout-minutes`, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of the empty "no failed-step log" shrug.
3. **Root-cause dedup**: before filing, match the extracted error signature (normalized, e.g. the server message / ::error:: text hash) against open issues' bodies/comments; if a match exists, comment on that issue with the new run link instead of filing a new one. Leg-title dedup alone is not enough (#1452 vs #1473).
4. Keep the existing auto-close-on-green and dedup-by-open-leg-issue behavior.

## Tests

- Fixture-driven unit tests for the extractor: tree-noise log → quotes the server message; cancelled-run log set → cancelled section with job+ceiling; no-signal log → tail fallback.
- Dedup test: open issue containing the same signature → comment, not new issue.
- The `inject_failure` TEST hook in daily-publish.yml already exercises the filing path end-to-end — extend it to assert the excerpt content, not just issue creation.

## Evidence

- #1472 body (empty digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- #1473 body (tree-noise digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1473#issuecomment-6095262585
- Root cause already open elsewhere: #1452

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38035614278) · started 07:48 · done 08:33 ✅
- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38040011389) · started 09:05 · done 09:17 ✅

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)

    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line

}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m

  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {

      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
}

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id
  local title="[daily-publish] $1 leg failed"
  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ leg \`$1\` went green again in $daily_url — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    actions+="auto-closed #${existing} ($1 green again)"$'\n'
  fi
}

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"
}

# Plan job: a failure here means legs never ran correctly — it gets its own
# issue instead of escaping the self-healing loop.
if [ "${PLAN_RESULT:-success}" != "success" ]; then
  file_or_comment plan "Plan (change detection + versions)" ""
  failed_legs+="plan "
  echo "| Plan | - | ❌ ${PLAN_RESULT} | [daily run]($daily_url) |" >> "$rows"
else
  close_if_open plan
fi

# pub.dev status override — display names MUST match the workflow job names
# exactly ("Leg: <name>"): the log-prefix filter relies on them.
pubdev_override=""
case "${LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS:-}" in
  private)    pubdev_override="private (publish_to: none)";;
  recovered)  pubdev_override="recovered — tag-publish rerun, pub.dev serves ${LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED:-?}";;
  up-to-date) pubdev_override="up-to-date (pub.dev serves ${LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED:-?})";;

  release-in-flight) pubdev_override="skipped: release in flight (tag-publish outcome unobserved this run; the next daily re-verifies)";;
esac

process_leg cli "CLI + macOS desktop" "${LEG_CLI:-}" "${LEG_CLI_URL:-}" \

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1480
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1480
- **Title**: gh-1478 [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1478` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +870
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:33:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T09:21:18Z

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1480._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: test gap — no coverage for the CLI leg's ceiling lookup**

The cancelled-leg test only exercises the TestFlight shape, and the wiring test greps for the mere presence of the `leg_ceiling_minutes` string — so the regex bug above (CLI fragment with `+` never matches the workflow yaml) passes CI silently. A small addition would have caught it:

```dart
test('ceiling lookup handles the CLI leg name with a literal +', () {
  final r = runReport(
    'cancelled-cli',
    legResults: const {'cli': 'cancelled'},
    fixtures: const {'run-555.json': _run555Jobs},
    withWorkflowYaml: true,
  );
  expect(r.createdBody, contains('Timeout ceiling'),
      reason: 'the CLI leg name contains + which must match literally');
});
```

Alternatively (or additionally) assert in the existing wiring test that the fixture yaml's `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` ceiling (360) is resolvable.

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `fmt_elapsed` doc comment promises zero-padding the code doesn't produce**

The comment says `-> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"`, but the arithmetic emits unpadded components: 3723s renders as `1h2m3s`, not `1h02m03s`. Purely cosmetic (the cancelled-digest readers won't care), but the comment documents a format the code doesn't implement — either pad (`printf '%dh%02dm%02ds'`) or fix the comment to say `1h2m3s`.

---

### Thread 5

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# gh-1478: [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)

## Description

## Problem

The daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh` + the Summary job) files issues whose "Last lines of the failed step's log" are systematically useless — proven twice in one morning (2026-10-10):

1. **#1472** (testflight): the leg run was `cancelled` (job hit its own timeout mid-checkout) → digest body says *"(no failed-step log available — see the run link)"*. A cancelled job produces no failed step, so the one thing the reader needs — WHICH job hit WHAT limit — is absent.
2. **#1473** (pubdev): the digest quoted the `dart pub publish` **file-tree listing** as the tail; the actual failure — `Message from server: CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)` — sat one screen above. The extractor grabbed noise over signal.
3. **No root-cause dedup**: #1473 re-filed a failure whose root cause was already open as #1452 (CHANGELOG > 256 KiB). Same failure will re-file every day until #1452 lands, spamming the tracker with symptom duplicates.

## Requirements

1. **Signal-first excerpt**: when building the digest, grep the failed job's log for `::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines (priority order) and quote the first matches with a few lines of context; fall back to the raw tail only when no signal line exists.
2. **Cancelled-run handling**: a leg whose run concluded `cancelled` gets a dedicated digest section — which job was in flight, its `timeout-minutes`, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of the empty "no failed-step log" shrug.
3. **Root-cause dedup**: before filing, match the extracted error signature (normalized, e.g. the server message / ::error:: text hash) against open issues' bodies/comments; if a match exists, comment on that issue with the new run link instead of filing a new one. Leg-title dedup alone is not enough (#1452 vs #1473).
4. Keep the existing auto-close-on-green and dedup-by-open-leg-issue behavior.

## Tests

- Fixture-driven unit tests for the extractor: tree-noise log → quotes the server message; cancelled-run log set → cancelled section with job+ceiling; no-signal log → tail fallback.
- Dedup test: open issue containing the same signature → comment, not new issue.
- The `inject_failure` TEST hook in daily-publish.yml already exercises the filing path end-to-end — extend it to assert the excerpt content, not just issue creation.

## Evidence

- #1472 body (empty digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- #1473 body (tree-noise digest), RCA: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1473#issuecomment-6095262585
- Root cause already open elsewhere: #1452

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    $0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h02m03s"
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do

}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"

        cs=$(date -u -d "$cstart" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        ce=$(date -u -d "$cend" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"

Fixed — the verify step no longer fires on scheduled runs.

The step's `if` is now:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

On `schedule` triggers the `inputs` context is empty, so `inputs.inject_failure` is `''` and the new `!= ''` term keeps the step skipped on every cron run; on `workflow_dispatch` the `default: none` still applies and both terms pass for a real injection. A comment above the step documents why the `!= ''` guard exists so it isn't "simplified" back.

Regression coverage: the wiring test in `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart` now asserts the yaml contains `inputs.inject_failure != ''` with a reason explaining the empty-inputs-on-schedule behavior — the test fails if the gate regresses to `!= 'none'` only.

Fixed — `leg_ceiling_minutes` now matches the job-name fragment **literally** instead of interpolating it into an unescaped awk ERE:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") > 0 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` in `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` is now an ordinary character. One adjustment to the suggested fix: the real `daily-publish.yml` has job names indented four spaces, so `index($0, "name: ") == 1` (column 1) would itself have missed every leg — the fix uses `> 0` and stays anchored to `name: ` lines so `timeout-minutes:` values can't self-match.

Verified live against the real yaml — all six legs now resolve (was: CLI empty):

- `Leg: TestFlight` → 360
- `Leg: Play` → 240
- `Leg: pub.dev` → 60
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → 360
- `Leg: Website` → 180
- `Leg: Outlook add-in` → 150

Regression test: new `cancelled-cli` test in `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart` cancels the CLI leg job and asserts the digest carries `Timeout ceiling` + `360` — it fails on the old regex (confirmed RED before the fix).

This test fails against the pre-fix awk regex (the `+` never matched the yaml), so the gap that let the bug pass CI is now closed — the existing TestFlight-only shape plus this one cover both fragment forms (plain and `+`-bearing, no parenthetical).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1480
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1480
- **Title**: gh-1478 [ENH] daily-publish auto-filer: signal-first failure excerpts + cancelled-run digests + root-cause dedup (never-again for noise filings)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1478` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +870
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T08:33:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T09:21:18Z

## PR Description

Closes #1478
### What changed
Reworked the daily-publish self-filer (`scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`) to file signal-bearing digests: failure excerpts are now grep-first (`::error::`, `Message from server`, `error:`, `FAIL`, exit-code lines, quoted with context; raw tail only as fallback), cancelled legs get a dedicated section (job in flight, `timeout-minutes` ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling from the jobs API + workflow yaml), and a normalized error signature is searched against open issues' bodies/comments so a known root cause gets a comment instead of a daily symptom duplicate. The `inject_failure` TEST hook now asserts the filed issue quotes the injected `::error::` line via a new report-job step.

### Key decisions
- Own-run/mid-run logs use the **per-job log endpoint** (`gh run view --job <id> --log`): the run-level zip is 409 mid-run, which is what produced the #1472 empty shrug; this also makes the `inject_failure` excerpt assertion possible.
- Signature = first line of the highest-priority signal class, stripped of gh log prefixes/timestamps; embedded in filed bodies as `<!-- daily-publish-sig: … -->` and matched via `gh search issues --match body,comments` (hits comments, any label — #1452 is not `daily-publish`).
- Excerpt window: first 3 signal matches ±3 lines (merged), tail capped at 400 lines / 50-line fallback; title dedup and auto-close-on-green are untouched and regression-tested.
- `DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW` env seam for the ceiling lookup so the script stays shell-harness testable.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart
```
Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10089 passed, 10 skipped.

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[Failed/cancelled leg] --> FS[failing steps via jobs API]
  LEG --> LE[log_excerpt]
  LE -->|child run| CF[gh run view --log-failed]
  LE -->|own run / mid-run| PJ[gh run view --job id --log]
  CF --> SE[signal_excerpt: first 3 signal matches +/-3 ctx]
  PJ --> SE
  SE -->|no signal| TAIL[raw tail fallback]
  SE --> SIG[error_signature: priority-class line, normalized]
  SIG --> SEARCH[gh search issues --match body,comments]
  SEARCH -->|match| CMT[comment on root-cause issue]
  SEARCH -->|no match| TITLE[leg-title dedup -> comment or file]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1480._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: verify step runs (and fails) on every scheduled daily run**

`inject_failure` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only input (`default: none`). On `schedule` triggers — the primary daily use of this workflow — the GitHub Actions `inputs` context is **empty**, so `inputs.inject_failure` evaluates to `''`, not `'none'`. Therefore:

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

is **true on every cron run**. The step then computes `title="[daily-publish]  leg failed"` (empty `INJECTED`), finds no such open issue, and hits `exit 1` — turning the report job (and thus the whole daily run) red **every single day**, even when all legs are green. The dispatch default only applies to `workflow_dispatch` events; it does not populate `inputs` for `schedule`.

The existing leg hooks use `== 'testflight'` etc., which is safe precisely because empty never equals a leg name — the `!= 'none'` form inverts that safety.

Fix (either):

```yaml
if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
```

or guard in-script (more robust against any future trigger that lacks inputs):

```bash
[ -n "${INJECTED}" ] || { echo "no inject_failure input — nothing to verify"; exit 0; }
```

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `leg_ceiling_minutes` silently misses the CLI leg — the awk regex breaks on `+` in the fragment**

`file_or_comment` derives the fragment with `frag="${prefix%% (*}"`, which only strips a ` (` parenthetical. For the CLI leg the report display is `CLI + macOS desktop` (no parenthetical), so `frag` is the literal `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop`. That string is then interpolated **unescaped** into an awk ERE:

```awk
$0 ~ ("name: ." frag) { injob = 1; next }
```

`+` is a regex operator, so the pattern `name: .Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` can never match the workflow line `name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'` — after the space-run matched by ` +`, the pattern demands `macOS` but the text has `+ macOS`. Verified against the real `daily-publish.yml`:

- `Leg: TestFlight` → `360` ✅
- `Leg: Play` → `240` ✅
- `Leg: pub.dev` → `60` ✅
- `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` → **empty** ❌

Result: a cancelled CLI leg gets "Cancelled while running: job … killed after X elapsed." with **no timeout ceiling and no elapsed-vs-ceiling verdict** — an AC2 gap for one of the six legs (and the new test's fixture yaml uses `Leg: CLI + macOS desktop` as a job name but never asserts its ceiling, so the gap is invisible in CI).

Fix — match the fragment literally instead of as a regex, e.g.:

```awk
index($0, "name: ") == 1 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
```

or escape `frag` with `gsub(/[][\\.^$*+?()|]/, "\\\\&", frag)` before building the pattern.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/daily_publish_report_signal_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: test gap — no coverage for the CLI leg's ceiling lookup**

The cancelled-leg test only exercises the TestFlight shape, and the wiring test greps for the mere presence of the `leg_ceiling_minutes` string — so the regex bug above (CLI fragment with `+` never matches the workflow yaml) passes CI silently. A small addition would have caught it:

```dart
test('ceiling lookup handles the CLI leg name with a literal +', () {
  final r = runReport(
    'cancelled-cli',
    legResults: const {'cli': 'cancelled'},
    fixtures: const {'run-555.json': _run555Jobs},
    withWorkflowYaml: true,
```
